notes: Prototype data for native-2026, round 3. Episodes (title, show, hook, duration, artwork_url, subject) are sampled from data/discover.json; subject labels and show counts come from data/taxonomy.json and discover.json; forays come from data/forays.json (titles, clip order, clip lengths; show names and feed URLs from data/segment-sources.json). Authored for the prototype: why-lines, the narration lines in the lead foray, bridge sentences, playlist names, the library seed. Every foray cover is the real cover of the show named beside it: shows outside the committed catalog were resolved once through the iTunes Search API (feed URL matched against segment-sources.json, artworkUrl600) and stored in each foray's show_art; there are no stand-ins. tones maps each cover URL to its vivid-first oklch hue (h), mean chroma (c), mean lightness (l) and the share of vivid pixels (v), canvas-extracted at 24x24 (the shipped app extracts them at runtime). data.js is the same object as data.json, loadable under file://.

forays.title: Barbecue: eight stories from a much longer history
forays.summary: Fire, satay, asado and jerk, then who cooked America's barbecue and who was credited for it.
forays.why: Picked because you finished a grilling episode. Six shows, one story, joined by short links.
forays.subject: Grilling & barbecue

clips.label: ORI-1
clips.gist: Cooking selected for smaller teeth and guts; chimps chew up to six hours daily, we chew one.

clips.label: ORI-2
clips.gist: Controlled fire is hard to prove; Wonderwerk Cave pushes it back a million years.

clips.label: SATAY-1
clips.gist: Three rival origin theories for satay, then the point that skewered meat is universal

clips.label: ARG-1
clips.gist: Asado is not a meal but a way of living — a four-to-six-hour party, every occasion.

clips.label: ARG-2
clips.gist: Argentina's grill has a firebox at the side; you cook once the embers glow red.

clips.label: JERK-1
clips.gist: Jerk began as preservation — wood ash instead of salt, a pit, and pimento wood smoke.

clips.label: GC-1
clips.gist: Miller names the tasks, and says plainly why enslaved African Americans were made to do them

clips.label: GC-2
clips.gist: Miller's sources are old newspapers, and he dates when they began naming the cook

clips.label: MOSS-1
clips.gist: American barbecue took root in Virginia, then rode west with the settlers to gold-rush California.

clips.label: MOSS-2
clips.gist: Barbecue faded after the war, revived in the 1990s; the German mustard story is doubtful.

narration: Next: where cooking may have started.
Satay's origin is argued over, and nobody agrees.
Now the Argentine answer: fire at the side.
Back to the pit, with a Jamaican method.
Next: who cooked, and who got the credit.
Then the American story, from Virginia west.
One more voice on how the story faded.
Last: the revival, and the mustard myth.
That is the full arc, from fire to a backyard grill.

forays.title: How Earth got plate tectonics and Venus never did
forays.summary: Water, sinking slabs and two blobs at the bottom of the mantle: the machine that moves continents.
forays.why: Geologists on how plates started. Follows the volcano story you played.
forays.subject: Earth Science

clips.label: FACC-1
clips.gist: Faccenna defines a subduction zone: cold dense plate sinking into mantle honey, resisted by viscosity and bending.

clips.label: BERC-1
clips.gist: Cooling makes ocean plates heavier but also stronger, so in principle Earth should have no subduction zones.

clips.label: ELK-1
clips.gist: How traces of water inside crystals soften Earth's interior enough for plate tectonics, and why Venus stiffened

clips.label: CAW-1
clips.gist: Cawood describes the stagnant-lid Earth before plates: scattered volcanism, catastrophic crustal overturn, a mantle hundreds of degrees hotter

clips.label: BREN-1
clips.gist: Brenner measured 3.48-billion-year-old Pilbara rocks shifting from Berlin's latitude to Svalbard's, proving two plates already moved separately

clips.label: CAW-2
clips.gist: Cawood dates global plate tectonics to 3.2-2.5 billion years, and explains why Venus and Mars never got it

clips.label: VH-1
clips.gist: Van Hinsbergen contrasts Holmes's boiling-milk mantle with slab pull, and why seismic imaging can finally test both.

clips.label: VH-2
clips.gist: Evidence that the mantle barely moves, so plates drive themselves rather than riding convection cells.

clips.label: VH-3
clips.gist: Australia and India lost their slabs and kept moving; the slab-pull prediction fails on real plate histories.

clips.label: MCN-1
clips.gist: McNamara likens seismic tomography to a CAT scan, and explains why quakes and stations leave big gaps

clips.label: ROM-1
clips.gist: Romanowicz traces subducted slabs down to a ring of fast rock circling two huge slow blobs

clips.label: MCN-2
clips.gist: Mid-ocean ridge basalts share one chemistry; hotspot basalts differ, hinting the two lower-mantle blobs feed them

clips.label: ROM-2
clips.gist: Tethys slabs sit under India and Tibet, and the lost Farallon plate reaches the core boundary

clips.label: MCN-3
clips.gist: Ultra-low velocity zones act like sand in a swimming pool, and may be sunken banded iron formations

clips.label: JOHN-1
clips.gist: Three ways to rust the early ocean's iron: ultraviolet light, photosynthetic oxygen, or iron-eating anoxygenic bacteria

clips.label: JOHN-2
clips.gist: Preston Cloud said rivers carried the iron; vent chemistry moved the source offshore, then isotopes moved it back

clips.label: EVAN-1
clips.gist: Evans traces the self-organizing cycle: colliding continents shut off subduction, mantle heats, and the supercontinent splits apart.

clips.label: NANC-1
clips.gist: Seismic tomography found slabs reaching the core-mantle boundary and an LLSVP sitting under Pangaea's old position.

clips.label: EVAN-2
clips.gist: Australia is heading for Taiwan; Evans names the next supercontinent Amasia and dates the collision.
